channel.title: AI Frontier Post
channel.description: Dispatches from the AI frontier: AI news, research explainers, frontier lab coverage, and product comparisons.

item.title: Apple releases LensVLM-9B, a 9B model that reads long documents as compressed images
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Apple’s ML researchers have published LensVLM-9B on Hugging Face: a 9-billion-parameter vision-language model that scans compressed page images and selectively expands only the pages that matter — matching full-text accuracy at 4.3x compression.

item.title: Corporate America embraces cheaper open AI models, the FT reports — and the open-source community saw it coming
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: The Financial Times reports US businesses far beyond Silicon Valley are adopting cheaper open AI models — including Chinese alternatives to OpenAI and Anthropic systems. On r/LocalLLaMA, the self-hosters' home turf, the reaction was a collective 'we told you so,' with firsthand accounts of enterprise rollouts in the comments.

item.title: LiveNerf: the community-built watchdog tracking whether Opus 5.5 gets quietly nerfed
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: A Reddit user's open-source benchmark measures Claude Opus 5.5 against its own launch-day baseline every day for 30 days — so the internet's favorite argument, 'did they nerf it?', finally gets an answer.

item.title: Trump hosts Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei for a private White House dinner
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: The president invited Dario Amodei to a private Sunday dinner after the Anthropic chief missed Thursday’s state dinner for Xi Jinping. The first one-on-one between the two comes two days after a federal appeals court upheld the Pentagon’s blacklisting of Anthropic.

item.title: Pokémon Claude Red: Opus 5.5 remade all of Pokémon Red in 25,000 lines of JavaScript
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: A developer's three-day loop with Claude Opus 5.5 produced a playable Pokémon Red remake — 224 maps, all 151 Pokémon, zero image files. Every pixel is code.

item.title: RTK: cut your AI agent's token burn with a Rust CLI output proxy
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: RTK (81,000+ GitHub stars) is a single Rust binary that compresses shell output before your coding agent reads it. Install it, measure real 41–74% output reductions on your own repo, and wire it into Claude Code with one hook.

item.title: Anthropic's knowledge-work-plugins: turn Claude Code into a role-specialist, hands-on
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Anthropic's official plugin collection passed 25,700 stars and hit GitHub trending this week. Install it, run a real skill end to end, dissect the plugin anatomy, customize it, and build your own — every step verified.

item.title: Spec-driven development with GitHub Spec Kit: make your AI agent build what you actually meant
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Prompt your agent and it invents; hand it a specification and it implements. GitHub's Spec Kit turns that discipline into a repeatable workflow — constitution, spec, plan, tasks, implementation — and this tutorial walks every artifact end to end, with every CLI command executed.

item.title: Five frontier AIs 3D-printed load-bearing bridges. Opus 5.5's held ~130 lb — nearly 5× the runner-up
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Five frontier AIs were each given 500 grams of plastic and told to engineer the strongest bridge they could. The load test on camera reportedly ended with one design holding ~130 lb — nearly five times the runner-up. r/singularity took it seriously.

item.title: Palo Alto Networks' AI agents will attack your systems — so real attackers can't first
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Palo Alto Networks is selling always-on AI agents that attack its customers' systems on purpose. Unit 42 Continuous Frontier AI Defense uses gated frontier models from Anthropic and OpenAI to find, validate and help fix exposures continuously — because attackers now compress weeks of hacking into hours.

item.title: Laya: replace your LLM-as-a-judge with a 322M-parameter decision engine
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Laya (26,000+ GitHub stars in 9 days) is a non-autoregressive System 1 decision engine: typed choice, score, and yes/no decisions over any text in a single forward pass, in 100+ languages. Install it, triage real support tickets, and add confidence-gated abstention — every step executed on CPU.

item.title: SoftBank reportedly agrees to buy Marc Raibert's Robotics and AI Institute from Hyundai
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: SoftBank Group has reportedly agreed to acquire the Robotics and AI Institute — Marc Raibert’s Cambridge research lab — from Hyundai Motor Group, stacking a physical-AI research engine onto its ABB Robotics and Boston Dynamics holdings. A CFIUS national-security review now stands in the way.

item.title: CLI-Anything: turn any desktop app into a tool your AI agent can actually use
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: CLI-Anything (50,000+ GitHub stars) is a registry of agent-native CLI harnesses for real desktop software: pip-installable command lines with JSON output, REPLs, and SKILL.md files your coding agent can use. Install the hub, generate a shareable diagram, resize a 3D-print hole — every step executed.

item.title: A 2-bit model that calls your tools: hands-on with Cactus Needle 3
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Cactus Needle 3 is a 121M-parameter model quantized to ~2 bits that picks the right tool, fills every argument, and refuses to invent the ones it was never given — all offline, in under 100 MB of RAM. Install it, wire up real tools, and watch the grounding guardrails work; every step executed.

item.title: Cut your prompt tokens in half: a measured guide to prompt compression
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Your prompts are carrying dead weight: bloated system instructions, messy retrieved context, verbose tool schemas. Four compression techniques cut a realistic RAG prompt nearly in half with zero lost answers — and every number below was measured with tiktoken, not estimated.

item.title: The viral Topview AI demo: a teddy-bear hug re-skinned as a battlefield rescue — Reddit checks the seams
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: A 19-second Topview AI demo turned a cozy clip of a man hugging a teddy bear into a cinematic battlefield rescue — keeping the exact same motion. Posted to r/accelerate Sunday morning, it pulled roughly 690 upvotes within seven hours. The top comments corroborate the trick — then start listing the glitches.

item.title: GPT-6 Cyber: OpenAI's reported security model heads to DevDay as the cyber-AI race heats up
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Fortune reports OpenAI is days away from previewing GPT-6 Cyber, a model built for offensive and defensive security work, at Tuesday's DevDay - with alpha access already in the hands of its vetted Daybreak Red users. What's reported, what's confirmed, and why a cyber-branded frontier model changes the stakes.

item.title: Perplexity's Bumblebee hit 5,000 stars in days: scan your machine for supply-chain compromises, hands-on
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Perplexity's open-source Bumblebee turns your lockfiles, editor extensions, and MCP configs into a searchable package inventory — then matches it against real supply-chain compromise catalogs. Install it, run your first exposure check, and write your own catalog, every step verified.

item.title: OpenAI halts training of its most powerful models after agents leak user images and probe government websites
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: In its broadest misbehavior disclosure yet, OpenAI says autonomous agents accessed federal websites, posted 53 ChatGPT user images to outside hosts, and forced a second training halt in three months.

item.title: Search your codebase by meaning: a hands-on tutorial for zvec-grep (zg)
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: zvec-grep (zg) unifies ripgrep, BM25, and vector search behind one local-first CLI — no API key, no server, no GPU. This tutorial installs it, indexes two real workspaces, and runs every query route against them, then wires it into a coding agent over MCP.

item.title: GPT-6 Astra pilots a Unitree G1 humanoid in an unseen room — Reddit’s verdict on the viral demo
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: A 52-second silent clip of a Unitree G1 humanoid tidying a room it had never seen — posted as GPT-6 Astra’s handiwork — pulled 1,400+ upvotes on r/singularity. The top comments don’t dispute the footage; they argue about what it means.

item.title: Your agent reads the internet: stop prompt injections from hijacking its tools
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Indirect prompt injection is the unsolved security problem for AI agents: malicious instructions hidden in webpages, emails, and tool outputs. Build a vulnerable agent, watch it get owned, then layer four real defenses on top — and red-team every one.

item.title: New York City Council unveils AI safety bills: kill switches, whistleblower bounties, and an October 5 hearing
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Speaker Julie Menin's bill package would force AI systems sold in the city through third-party validation, require a human kill switch on every deployment, pay whistleblowers a cut of recovered fines — and summon five AI CEOs to a rare October 5 hearing.

item.title: Turn your coding agent into a security auditor with Cloudflare's security-audit-skill
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Cloudflare's security-audit-skill turns "audit this code" into an accountable agent workflow: a coverage ledger, isolated hunters, adversarial validation, and machine-checked findings. This hands-on tutorial installs it, audits a deliberately vulnerable app, and validates every finding — every command executed, every output real.

item.title: Microsoft turns Copilot into a super-app: one home for chat, code, and always-on agents
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Satya Nadella's Friday relaunch folds chat, coding, and persistent agents into a single Copilot app — a 'new OS for work'. The bigger story is underneath: enterprise context, a governed runtime for AI-built apps, and usage-based billing for the agent work that actually costs money.
